key_insight: A privacy-preserving Llama 3.3 70B pipeline accurately extracted oncology registry variables from clinical notes without task-specific fine-tuning.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support oncology registry abstraction for research and care documentation; it did not evaluate cancer drug discovery or patient outcomes.
method: Extracted over 50 variables from 6,700 oncology notes at a Singapore cancer centre.
De-identified notes locally using a Hide-In-Plain-Sight approach, keeping identifiable data within hospital infrastructure.
Classified outputs as correct, missing, spurious, or incorrect against an adjudicated reference standard.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on 200 randomly sampled notes yielded F1 scores of 97.2% for diagnosis, 95.8% for histology, 92.6% for stage, 91.4% for biomarkers, and 88.1% for treatments.
watch_item: Transferability testing was preliminary, involving only 50 external notes, with reduced performance for list-valued variables.
paper_title: Privacy-Preserving Large Language Model Deployment for Oncology Registry Abstraction: Structure-Aware Evaluation in a Real-World Clinical Setting
